newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST - Beer volumes key to FEMSA's Q3.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Beer volumes key to FEMSA's Q3.

text.p: Beverage analysts said they would be keeping a close eye on beer division sales volumes when bottler Fomento Economico Mexican (FEMSA) reports its third-quarter earnings, which are due out later Wednesday.

Monterrey-based FEMSA, which also owns the Coca-Cola FEMSA SA distributorship of the soft drink in Mexico and Brazil, bottles the Cuauhtemoc Moctezuma beers such as Sol, Tecate, Carta Blanca and Dos Equis.
FEMSA's beer division posted a sales volume of 14.047 million hectoliters in the first nine months of 1995, which was a 4.8 percent drop from 1994.
The big challenge for FEMSA is to increase volume by 10 percent to match rising soft-drink volumes and expected increases of arch rival Grupo Modelo. Few predict FEMSA will come close, though.

"I think basically people are going to be looking for some sense of recovery in volumes," said Marla Marron, analyst with Salomon Brothers in New York. "That's the most important thing right now because it's clear that there is not going to be any price increase yet."
Sales of soft drinks and beer tumbled in Mexico following the economic crisis prompted by the December 1994 peso crash.
FEMSA's soft drinks division has rebounded, but the beer division has lagged.
By the same token, beer-makers have been unable to raise prices much because of lingering effects from the crisis.
Marron said FEMSA volumes could grow by three percent to five percent, but then backed off, saying "five percent is too aggressive."
Jose Yordan, analyst with CS First Boston in New York, agreed that volume was the key issue and predicted a more bold eight percent increase.
"Coke FEMSA's already, reported, so there's no mystery there," he said. "And Modelo's been talking about 10 percent growth in volume, so I think volume growth in the beer sector will be important."
